content.value_statement: Validation bugs create weak application boundaries and unclear user errors. This skill gives practical Zod patterns for TypeScript schemas, API validation, transforms, and typed results.
actual_capabilities: Defines reusable Zod schemas for emails, passwords, URLs, dates, identifiers, payment fields, and common business data.
Shows safe parsing, custom error maps, formatted errors, and field-level error output for forms and APIs.
Covers refinements, superRefine, conditional rules, cross-field validation, and business-rule validation.
Explains transforms and preprocessing for numbers, booleans, URLs, JSON strings, names, and normalized inputs.
Includes async validation examples for database checks, DNS checks, external API checks, caching, and batching.
Documents type inference patterns using z.infer, input and output types, discriminated unions, and schema composition.
limitations: The skill is documentation and examples. It does not validate a project automatically.
Some async examples use placeholder external services and must be adapted before production use.
The guidance assumes TypeScript and Zod are already part of the project.
External validation of sensitive data still needs a privacy and security review.

use_cases.title: Validate API Requests
use_cases.description: Create Zod schemas for Next.js routes, Server Actions, and request payloads before business logic runs.

use_cases.title: Improve Form Errors
use_cases.description: Turn Zod validation failures into clear field messages, formatted errors, and localized user feedback.

use_cases.title: Standardize Shared Schemas
use_cases.description: Build common validation modules for identifiers, contact details, addresses, payments, dates, and typed data contracts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Zod schema for this TypeScript data model. Include required fields, optional fields, clear messages, and inferred types.

prompt_templates.title: Add Form Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Zod validation patterns to design form validation for this submission. Include safe parsing and user-friendly field errors.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cross-Field Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Zod refinements for these cross-field rules. Explain which rules belong in refine, superRefine, or separate service checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Validation Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this validation layer for schema reuse, transforms, async checks, type inference, error handling, and unsafe validation gaps.

output_examples.input: A user asks for registration validation with email, password, display name, and age rules.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a schema design with field rules, password constraints, age bounds, safe parsing guidance, and inferred TypeScript types.

output_examples.input: A user asks why form errors are hard to render consistently.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends formatted Zod errors, field-level message mapping, custom error text, and a predictable response shape.

output_examples.input: A user asks to validate webhook events from several event types.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests discriminated unions, boundary validation, typed handlers, and explicit handling for unknown or invalid event payloads.

best_practices: Validate all untrusted data at application boundaries before business logic uses it.
Use safeParse for request and form flows so failures return structured errors instead of thrown exceptions.
Keep async validation endpoints configurable, timeout-bound, and reviewed for privacy impact.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on TypeScript types alone for runtime data from users, APIs, forms, or files.
Do not send sensitive user data to third-party validators without consent and a privacy review.
Do not hide major business rules inside transforms that silently change user-provided values.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design Zod schemas, error handling, transforms, refinements, async validation, API integration, and TypeScript type inference.

faq.question: Does it execute validation code for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples that an AI assistant can use while writing or reviewing project code.

faq.question: Can it be used with Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation includes patterns for API routes, Server Actions, form data, file uploads, and response formatting.

faq.question: Does it cover custom business rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers refine, superRefine, conditional validation, cross-field validation, and domain-specific rule examples.

faq.question: Does it include async validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes database checks, DNS checks, external API checks, timeout handling, caching, debouncing, and batching examples.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive data workflows?
faq.answer: It can guide validation design, but sensitive data workflows still need privacy controls, storage rules, and security review.
